claims.text: Uncertainty quantification in free-form responses from large language models is challenging due to difficulty defining task-specific uncertainties.
Characterizing utility as a similarity measure comparing generated and hypothetical true responses enables principled quantification of subjective uncertainty and calibration.
Epistemic uncertainty in language models can be derived from a missing data perspective and characterized as excess risk.
The proposed uncertainty quantification methods are applicable to black-box language models.
Epistemic uncertainty provides a promising deferral strategy for efficient data acquisition in in-context learning.

evidence.description: Applications of large language models often involve the generation of free-form responses, in which case uncertainty quantification becomes challenging. This is due to the need to identify task-specific uncertainties (e.g., about the semantics) which appears difficult to define in general cases.

This work addresses these challenges from a perspective of Bayesian decision theory, starting from the assumption that our utility is characterized by a similarity measure that compares a generated response with a hypothetical true response. We discuss how this assumption enables principled quantification of the model's subjective uncertainty and its calibration.
We further derive a measure for epistemic uncertainty, based on a missing data perspective and its characterization as an excess risk.
The proposed methods can be applied to black-box language models.
Our experiments ... demonstrate that epistemic uncertainty offers a promising deferral strategy for efficient data acquisition in in-context learning.

methodologies.name: Bayesian Decision Theory Framework for NLG Uncertainty Quantification
methodologies.description: A framework that quantifies subjective and epistemic uncertainty in language generation by defining utility via a similarity measure comparing generated and hypothetical true responses.

limitations.text: Uncertainty quantification in natural language generation with free-form responses is challenging due to the difficulty of identifying task-specific uncertainties.
